newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian PM hopes Duma will back budget on Dec 15.
newsitem.headline: Russian PM hopes Duma will back budget on Dec 15.

text.p: Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin said on Tuesday he hoped Russia's 1997 draft budget would pass through its first reading in State Duma lower house parliament on December 15.
"We will continue discussing the budget on December 15 and I hope we will get it approved," Chernomyrdin said, addressing the upper house of parliament.
"We have to adopt the budget because the country cannot live in the first quarter of next year under the budget for the fourth quarter of 1996... We cannot allow that," he said.
The draft budget must pass through three readings in the Duma and win the approval of the upper chamber before President Boris Yeltsin can sign it into law.
If deputies fail to approve a new budget by the end of the year Russia will have to adopt interim budgets or re-use the 1996 law.
The 1997 draft forsees inflation of 11-12 percent and a budget deficit of 3.5 percent of Gross Domestic Product. Chernomyrdin said the government could not compromise on these basic indices.
"If we made them higher, capital would stay in the banking sector, and all (capital) growth would be eaten up by government securities," Chernomyrdin said.

Lawmakers, unable to agree on a blueprint for Russia's economic well-being, voted last week to delay further discussion of the 1997 budget to December 15 leaving less than three weeks before it was due to take effect.
The head of the Duma's budget committee Mikhail Zadornov told reporters on Tuesday the lower house was likely to approve the spending plan for 1997 on December 15.
The budget introduced by the government last week offered higher spending and higher income than earlier drafts.
